title: RA 8371 — Indigenous Peoples’ Rights Act (IPRA)
status: Binding national statute
context: All ICCs/IPs; knowledge, histories, institutions and territory
how: Recognizes community intellectual rights, oral traditions, Indigenous sciences and technologies, medicines, seeds and cultural expressions.
use: Community control; cultural transmission; education; resource stewardship; customary governance.
limits: Read §§3(g),(h),(i),13–17,21–28,29–37,51–52,58–59,63,65–66. §34 is central; §35 concerns biological/genetic resources. IPRA is broader than domain titling.
verif: Full statutory text inspected. Recognition of rights does not itself establish any particular project’s compliance.

title: 1987 Constitution
status: Binding constitutional law
how: Recognizes ICC rights and protection of ancestral lands; requires recognition, respect and protection of Indigenous cultural traditions and institutions.
use: Basis for cultural protection, participation and policy development.
limits: Art. II §22; Art. XII §5; Art. XIV §§14–18, especially §17. IPRA appears first here at the user’s request, without changing constitutional hierarchy.
verif: Full text inspected.

title: NCIP AO 1, s. 1998 — IPRA implementing rules
status: Binding implementing regulation, subject to later specific rules
context: Implementation of IPRA’s four bundles of rights
how: Details cultural integrity, community intellectual rights, self-governance and other rights recognized by IPRA.
use: Operational reference alongside the statute and subsequent subject-specific orders.
limits: Use relevant rules on cultural integrity and social justice. Do not treat the 1998 procedures as the only current procedures.
verif: Full official text available and relevant provisions inspected.

title: NCIP AO 1, s. 2012 — IKSPs and Customary Laws Research and Documentation Guidelines
status: Binding NCIP research/documentation regulation
context: Research involving IKSPs and customary laws
how: Provides community participation, consent processes, agreed terms, validation and benefit-sharing requirements, with different procedural routes.
use: Direct reference for interviews, oral accounts, community documentation and research outputs.
limits: Read scope/exceptions and procedure together; §§8–11 include community selection of informants, agreements and validation. Community approval of publication is material.
verif: Full official text inspected. Applicable route must be established for the actual activity.

title: NCIP AO 3, s. 2026 — The 2026 Guidelines on FPIC and Related Processes
status: New regulation listed by NCIP; operative clauses not inspected
how: NCIP’s official index records issuance on 28 September 2026; an October orientation announcement corroborates rollout.
use: Required current-law check before selecting a consent or certification procedure.
limits: Full text, publication/effectivity, repeal and transitional clauses were not retrieved. Do not infer the 2012 procedures remain controlling. Confirm the authenticated 2026 order before implementation.
verif: Official index and implementation announcement verified; full order not obtained.

title: NCIP AO 3, s. 2012 — Revised FPIC Guidelines
status: Earlier regulation; current application requires 2026 update check
how: Documents earlier consent and certification processes relevant to projects affecting ICCs/IPs.
use: Historical comparison and understanding of previous research or case records.
limits: Not presented as the sole current FPIC authority. Read PH05 and obtain the 2026 transition/repeal provisions.
verif: Earlier official publication identified; updated legal position is unresolved in this register.

title: Joint IPOPHL–NCIP AO 01, s. 2016 — protection of IP rights of ICCs/IPs
status: Binding joint administrative regulation
context: IP applications using IKSPs or associated cultural expressions
how: Provides origin disclosure, FPIC-related requirements and measures recognizing community ownership and custodianship.
use: Protection against unauthorized appropriation in intellectual-property applications.
limits: Rules 5–10 and 12; distinguish collective rights from eligibility for a particular patent, copyright or other statutory IP right.
verif: Full official text inspected. Not a general authorization to commercialize all documented knowledge.

title: RA 10066 — National Cultural Heritage Act of 2009
status: Binding national statute, as amended
how: Establishes heritage protection and cultural-agency responsibilities, including intangible heritage.
use: Safeguarding, inventory, heritage education and cultural institutions.
limits: Act is titled “of 2009” but enacted in 2010. Read with RA 11961 and its 2025 IRR, rather than only the original text.
verif: Full original statutory text inspected; amendments separately listed.

title: RA 11961 — cultural mapping amendment to RA 10066
status: Binding national statute
context: Community histories, cultural knowledge and practices
how: Requires cultural mapping and provides for ICC/IP participation in documenting origins, histories, institutions and diverse knowledge, subject to IPRA safeguards.
use: Strong basis for IKSP work extending beyond ancestral-domain dossiers.
limits: IP-driven documentation includes kinship, governance, customary law, technologies, healing and climate knowledge. Do not equate inventory with compulsory public disclosure.
verif: Statutory text inspected; implementation detail in PH10.

title: 2025 IRR of RA 11961
status: Binding implementing regulation
context: Cultural mapping by ICCs/IPs inside or outside ancestral domains
how: Section 65 expressly covers ICCs/IPs whether or not residing within ancestral domains; it addresses IP-driven mapping with IPRA safeguards.
use: Community archives, histories, languages, institutions and living knowledge in displaced or urban settings as well as territorial settings.
limits: §§21.9–21.9.1,64–65,70–71. §65.1 anticipates joint guidelines: this register does not assert that those separate guidelines have been issued.
verif: Full text and relevant provisions inspected. Registry interoperability does not remove consent restrictions.

title: DepEd Order 62, s. 2011 — National IP Education Policy Framework
status: Binding departmental education policy within its scope
how: Sets an institutional framework for culturally responsive education and engagement with ICCs/IPs.
use: Curriculum, community participation and educational access.
limits: Read with DO 32/2015 and DO 51/2014; policy existence is not evidence of implementation quality everywhere.
verif: Official issuance record identified; direct document access was blocked. Detailed clause-by-clause review pending.

title: DepEd Order 51, s. 2014 — activities and materials involving IP culture
status: Binding departmental education policy within its scope
context: School activities, representations and cultural materials
how: Addresses appropriate conduct and use of materials involving Indigenous cultures.
use: Teaching resources, cultural presentations and respectful representation.
limits: Relevant to turning oral accounts or rituals into learning materials; verify the complete enclosure before preparing materials.
verif: Official record identified; full enclosure could not be retrieved.

title: DepEd Order 32, s. 2015 — IP Education Curriculum Framework
status: Binding departmental education policy within its scope
how: Provides an IPEd curriculum framework for engagement with community contexts, knowledge and learning processes.
use: Place-based learning, community partnership and intergenerational knowledge transmission.
limits: Read with the National IPEd Policy Framework. This is educational policy, not a blanket research or publication consent.
verif: Official issuance record identified; full enclosure access blocked.

title: RA 10173 — Data Privacy Act
status: Binding national statute where personal-data processing is covered
context: Identifiable narrators, genealogies and ethnic affiliation
how: Regulates lawful processing, sensitive personal information, data-subject rights and security.
use: Protecting people recorded in interviews, family histories and digital archives.
limits: §3 on sensitive data; §§11–13,16,20. Individual data consent and collective community authorization address different rights; one does not automatically replace the other.
verif: Full statutory text inspected. Application and exceptions require attention to the actual processing.

title: RA 8293 — Intellectual Property Code, as amended
status: Binding national statute
context: Copyright, patents and other IP rights
how: Sets the statutory requirements and limits for forms of intellectual-property protection.
use: Licensing, authorship and assessment of misuse or appropriation risks.
limits: Read with amendments including RA 10372 and PH07. Copyright in a recording or text is not identical to ownership of the underlying community knowledge.
verif: Original text inspected; consolidated amendment-by-amendment review not completed.

title: RA 9147 — Wildlife Resources Conservation and Protection Act
status: Binding national statute; conditional sectoral application
how: Section 14 addresses bioprospecting and prior informed consent, including ICC consent in the circumstances specified.
use: Biodiversity research and access to biological resources.
limits: Apply with implementing rules, permitting and resource-specific jurisdiction; research documentation is not a collection permit.
verif: Full statutory text inspected.

title: Guidelines for Bioprospecting Activities in the Philippines — DENR/DA/PCSD/NCIP
status: Joint national regulation; sectoral application
context: Access to biological/genetic resources for bioprospecting
how: CBD’s national-measure record identifies consent procedures, agreements, benefit-sharing, monitoring and sanctions.
use: Access and benefit-sharing arrangements involving resources and associated knowledge.
limits: Adopted 14 January 2005; §13 PIC; §§14–22 benefit-sharing. CBD’s linked full-text file returned 404; obtain an authenticated full copy before operational use.
verif: Primary treaty-secretariat measure record inspected; full regulation not retrieved.

title: RA 8423 — Traditional and Alternative Medicine Act (TAMA)
status: Binding national statute
how: Creates PITAHC and a framework for research and development of traditional and alternative health care.
use: Documentation, evaluation and culturally responsive health research.
limits: Recognition and documentation of a practice do not establish clinical efficacy or safety. Read research and community rights together.
verif: Statutory text identified and relevant content inspected.

title: RA 10121 — Philippine Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Act
status: Binding national statute
context: Risk assessment, preparedness and community resilience
how: Policy includes sensitivity to Indigenous knowledge in disaster risk reduction.
use: Community warning knowledge, preparedness and locally grounded risk planning.
limits: §2(j). Integrate with hazard science and community assessment; do not assume every traditional indicator is a reliable forecast.
verif: Full statutory text inspected.

title: RA 9729 — Climate Change Act
status: Binding national statute, as amended
how: Establishes climate governance and participatory planning; relevant alongside documented Indigenous adaptation practices.
use: Local adaptation planning, livelihoods and ecosystem stewardship.
limits: Read with RA 10174 (2012) and applicable planning rules. This law alone does not authorize access to community knowledge.
verif: Full original statute inspected; later amendment is noted rather than exhaustively analyzed.

title: RA 11038 — Expanded NIPAS Act, amending RA 7586
status: Binding national statute; protected-area application
context: Overlap of protected areas and ancestral territories
how: Recognizes ICC/IP rights and responsibilities for governance and conservation in accordance with IKSPs and customary law.
use: Community conservation, protected-area planning and stewardship.
limits: Read provisions on ancestral domains and customary rights with IPRA and the site’s protected-area regime.
verif: Official statutory text/search-extracted provisions verified.

title: RA 9168 — Philippine Plant Variety Protection Act
status: Binding national statute; seeds/varieties application
context: Plant varieties and small-farmer seed practices
how: Provides plant variety protection with qualified exceptions for traditional small-farmer seed use and exchange.
use: Seed systems, crop diversity and farmers’ livelihoods.
limits: §43(d) is qualified, including commercial-reproduction limits; avoid describing it as an unlimited right to sell protected seed.
verif: Official statutory text/search-extracted provisions verified.

title: RA 7355 — Manlilikha ng Bayan Act
status: Binding national statute
how: Establishes recognition and support for National Living Treasures and development of traditional folk arts.
use: Transmission of artistic skills, support for cultural masters and public recognition.
limits: Institutional support for practitioners; an award does not transfer community ownership of designs or traditions.
verif: Official statutory record and provisions verified.

title: RA 9710 — Magna Carta of Women
status: Binding national statute
context: Indigenous women as rights holders and knowledge holders
how: Protects substantive equality and participation; explicitly recognizes Indigenous women and intersecting discrimination.
use: Women’s authority in knowledge documentation, education, resources and project decision-making.
limits: Read §§2–4 and provisions on participation, cultural identity and integrity. Community representation must be assessed alongside women’s rights.
verif: Full statutory text inspected.

title: Bangsamoro Autonomy Act 64 — Bangsamoro Indigenous Peoples’ Act of 2024
status: Binding regional statute within its jurisdiction
how: Regional law addresses collective rights, culture, traditions, institutions and political structures.
use: Region-specific legal framework for IKSP and customary institutions.
limits: Read alongside RA 11054, the Constitution, applicable national law and BIPA IRR. The register does not resolve jurisdictional overlaps.
verif: Official gazette and parliament records verified; full PDF access blocked.

title: BIPA implementing rules — BAA 64
status: Regional implementing rules; full terms not inspected
how: Official gazette lists implementing rules for the Bangsamoro Indigenous Peoples’ Act.
use: Necessary regional procedural check for work in BARMM.
limits: Listing verified as of 31 October 2026. Exact signature/effectivity date and operative clauses were not established; the year here denotes the verified 2026 listing, not a claimed adoption date.
verif: Existence/listing only; obtain authenticated full text before applying.

title: NCIP AO 2, s. 2012 — confirmation of Indigenous Political Structures and registration of Indigenous Peoples’ Organizations
status: Binding NCIP administrative regulation
context: Customary leadership, institutions and community organizations
how: Provides a framework recognizing Indigenous political structures and registering organizations.
use: Understanding community authority and governance when planning documentation and agreements.
limits: Political structures and registered organizations are distinct concepts; do not assume a researcher may select a convenient representative instead of following legitimate community processes.
verif: NCIP publication and CHR-hosted text identified; relevant introductory provisions verified.

title: NCIP AO 2, s. 2018 — Revised ADSDPP Guidelines
status: Binding NCIP planning regulation
context: Ancestral Domain Sustainable Development and Protection Plans
how: Provides a participatory planning framework for community development and protection priorities.
use: Linking IKSPs with territorial planning, livelihoods and community priorities when applicable.
limits: An ADSDPP is a territorial application of IKSPs; it does not define the outer limit of all IKSP work. Revises the 2004 guidelines.
verif: CHR-hosted NCIP text and 2025 DENR implementation reference verified; full clause-by-clause review pending.

title: NCIP AO 4, s. 2012 — Revised Omnibus Rules on Delineation and Recognition of Ancestral Domains and Lands
status: NCIP administrative regulation; subsequent amendments require checking
how: Details delineation/recognition processes for territorial claims.
use: Relevant where histories, genealogies or oral accounts support a domain/land claim.
limits: Do not extend a CADT/CALT evidence procedure into a universal test for Indigenous identity. A 2023 DA framework also cites AO 1, s.2020 with these rules; obtain amendments before filing.
verif: Official publication identified; current consolidated procedural text not fully reviewed.

title: NCIP AO 1, s. 2021 — Revised National Guidelines for mandatory IP representation
status: NCIP regulation; later amendments must be read together
context: Local legislative councils and policy-making bodies
how: Sets representation procedures supporting participation in public governance.
use: Context for whose knowledge and priorities inform public decisions.
limits: NCIP index identifies the 2021 revision; UP Law NARO records a 2023 amending issuance. This register does not claim an unamended 2021 text is the complete current rule.
verif: Official index and UP Law issuance registry verified: https://naro.law.upd.edu.ph/agencies/national-commission-on-indigenous-peoples

title: NCIP AO 1, s. 2018 — NCIP Rules of Procedure
status: Binding agency procedural rules within their jurisdiction
how: Provides agency procedure relevant to enforcing rights and addressing disputes.
use: Procedural context when IKSP, community authority or other IPRA-related disputes reach NCIP.
limits: Read with IPRA jurisdiction provisions and applicable court decisions. The existence of these rules does not establish NCIP jurisdiction over every dispute.
verif: Official NCIP issuance listing verified; full procedural text not inspected.

title: UN Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples (UNDRIP)
status: UN declaration; not itself a ratified treaty
how: Recognizes rights to maintain, control, protect and develop knowledge and cultural heritage.
use: Consent, cultural transmission and community authority.
limits: Arts.11–14,18–19,24,31–32. Distinguish the declaration’s status from binding treaty obligations and domestic IPRA rights.
verif: UN source and text identified.

title: Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD)
status: Binding treaty for the Philippines
how: Article 8(j) concerns knowledge relevant to conservation/sustainable use, approval/involvement of holders and equitable benefits; Art.10(c) concerns customary use.
use: Conservation, customary resource management and benefit-sharing.
limits: Subject to the treaty’s wording, including national legislation. PH party status: 6 January 1994.
verif: Treaty provision and CBD country status verified: https://www.cbd.int/countries?country=ph

title: Nagoya Protocol on Access and Benefit-sharing
status: Binding treaty for the Philippines
context: Genetic resources and associated traditional knowledge
how: Articles 7 and 12 address access to associated knowledge, community consent/approval, customary rules and protocols.
use: Research or commercial access and equitable benefit-sharing.
limits: Arts.5(5),7,12; not a universal instrument covering all unrelated cultural knowledge. PH party from 28 December 2015.
verif: Treaty text and CBD PH party status verified.

title: UNESCO Convention for the Safeguarding of the Intangible Cultural Heritage
status: Binding treaty for the Philippines
context: Living heritage including knowledge about nature and the universe
how: Defines safeguarding and calls for identification and participation by communities and practitioners.
use: Intergenerational transmission, community education and living cultural practices.
limits: Arts.2,11–15; PH ratification 18 August 2006. Inventory or inscription is not blanket consent for disclosure or reuse.
verif: UNESCO treaty text and state-party information verified.

title: International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights (ICCPR)
status: Binding treaty for the Philippines
how: Article 27 protects minority members’ enjoyment of culture with their community; Arts.1 and 26 add self-determination and equality parameters.
use: Cultural continuity and protection against discriminatory restrictions.
limits: State-party status is separate from whether a particular claim meets admissibility and domestic legal requirements.
verif: Treaty text identified; PH treaty status corroborated by government treaty records.

title: International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights (ICESCR)
status: Binding treaty for the Philippines
how: Article 15 recognizes participation in cultural life and benefits of science, with protection of authors’ interests.
use: Community cultural participation and equitable knowledge-related development.
limits: Read with Arts.1,2,13 and treaty-body interpretations; do not reduce collective IKSP rights to ordinary individual copyright.
verif: Official treaty text identified; PH party status corroborated by government records.

title: Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women (CEDAW)
status: Binding treaty for the Philippines
context: Women’s equality, participation and rural livelihoods
how: Provides a binding equality framework relevant to Indigenous women’s knowledge and participation.
use: Education, health, livelihood and decision-making rights.
limits: Arts.2,7,10–14. Pair with GR39 (IN08); the recommendation is an interpretation, not another treaty.
verif: Treaty record identified; PH party status corroborated by government records.

title: CEDAW General Recommendation 39 — rights of Indigenous women and girls
status: Treaty-body interpretive guidance; not a separate treaty
how: Explains State obligations affecting Indigenous women and girls, including participation and cultural rights.
use: Assessment of whose knowledge and decisions are represented in IKSP work.
limits: CEDAW/C/GC/39, 31 October 2022. Read with binding CEDAW and domestic equality obligations.
verif: Official UN document and identity verified; not treated as legislation.

title: Convention on the Rights of the Child (CRC)
status: Binding treaty for the Philippines
how: Articles 29 and 30 address cultural identity, language and Indigenous children’s enjoyment of culture.
use: Transmission to younger generations and culturally responsive learning.
limits: Apply children’s participation and protection requirements as well as community consent.
verif: Treaty record identified; PH party status corroborated by government records.

title: International Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Racial Discrimination (ICERD)
status: Binding treaty for the Philippines
context: Non-discrimination and equal enjoyment of rights
how: Article 5 covers equal cultural and other rights; CERD General Recommendation 23 interprets Indigenous Peoples’ concerns.
use: Addressing exclusion and discrimination affecting cultural practice and services.
limits: Distinguish binding convention from the interpretive recommendation; do not claim GR23 is a separate treaty.
verif: Treaty record identified; PH party status corroborated by government records.

title: Paris Agreement
status: Binding treaty for the Philippines; provisions differ in legal formulation
how: Article 7(5) explicitly includes traditional knowledge, knowledge of Indigenous Peoples and local knowledge systems as appropriate.
use: Participatory adaptation and resilience planning.
limits: The provision uses “should”; treaty status does not convert every phrase into an identical mandatory duty.
verif: UNFCCC official treaty resource identified; Article 7(5) is the relevant locator.

title: International Treaty on Plant Genetic Resources for Food and Agriculture
status: Binding treaty for the Philippines
how: Article 9 recognizes contributions of Indigenous/local communities and farmers, including relevant traditional knowledge.
use: Seed conservation, food security, participation and benefit-sharing.
limits: Art.9 implementation is subject to national law; PH entry into force 27 December 2006.
verif: FAO text and PH contracting-party record verified: https://www.fao.org/plant-treaty/countries/contracting-parties/detail/PHL/en

title: ILO Convention 169 — Indigenous and Tribal Peoples Convention
status: NOT ratified by the Philippines
how: Contains international standards on participation, culture, institutions and development priorities.
use: Comparative analysis and policy advocacy.
limits: Do not call it a binding Philippine treaty obligation. ILO’s current PH non-ratification record was checked.
verif: Official ILO status verified.

title: WIPO Treaty on IP, Genetic Resources and Associated Traditional Knowledge
status: Adopted treaty; NOT YET IN FORCE in WIPO register
context: Patent disclosure for inventions based on genetic resources/associated knowledge
how: Creates a disclosure framework upon entry into force; narrower than all traditional knowledge and cultural expressions.
use: Future/comparative patent-policy reference.
limits: WIPO register checked 31 October 2026: marked not yet in force; Philippines not listed among parties/signatories. Do not present as operative PH treaty law.
verif: Current official register inspected; adoption text: https://www.wipo.int/en/web/treaties/ip/gratk/index

title: Kunming–Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework
status: CBD COP decision/framework; not a separate ratified treaty
how: Targets 21 and 22 address knowledge access, community rights, consent and participation.
use: Policy assessment of conservation programmes and knowledge governance.
limits: Decision 15/4. Do not equate policy targets with an independently ratified statute or treaty.
verif: CBD framework and target text identified.

title: Sendai Framework for Disaster Risk Reduction 2015–2030
status: Non-binding international framework
how: Paragraph 24(i) calls for using traditional, Indigenous and local knowledge to complement scientific knowledge.
use: Risk assessment, preparedness and education.
limits: Policy benchmark; use Philippine DRRM law for domestic statutory obligations.
verif: UNDRR official framework record identified.

title: EMRIP study A/HRC/60/66 — Indigenous Peoples’ right to data
status: UN expert study/advice; not binding legislation
context: Data, collective knowledge governance and AI
how: Discusses Indigenous data rights, community information systems, traditional knowledge and digital technologies.
use: Assessment of community control over recording, repositories and AI-supported processing.
limits: Use the study as documented analysis and expert guidance; it does not itself grant permission to process any community’s data.
verif: Official UN study text inspected in the preceding project research; retrieval limitations remain for repeat PDF access.

title: Epanaw: Pagkilala (Recognize) — NCIP
status: Government coffee-table book; publisher scope verified
how: NCIP describes accounts of histories, locations, daily lives and social relations.
use: Context for community histories and diversity; locating people and themes for further research.
limits: Publisher describes the trilogy as covering 101 ICC/IP profiles. Full volume not obtained; not a verified comprehensive ethnography or identity-certification instrument.
verif: NCIP launch announcement and annual report identified; scope is publisher-described, not a full-book review.

title: Epanaw: Paggalang (Respect) — NCIP
status: Government coffee-table book; publisher scope verified
how: NCIP describes practices surrounding life events and agricultural cycles.
use: Cultural transmission and context for ceremonial or seasonal knowledge.
limits: Full volume not obtained. A public description of rituals is not evidence that restricted details may be reproduced or repurposed.
verif: Publisher announcement verified; full volume and bibliography not inspected.

title: Epanaw: Pagtaguyod (Promote) — NCIP
status: Government coffee-table book; publisher scope verified
how: NCIP describes places and tourism-related opportunities associated with ICCs/IPs and ancestral domains.
use: Context for livelihood, conservation and community-controlled cultural tourism.
limits: Full volume not obtained. Tourism promotion is not evidence of community consent to every visitor, recording or commercial use.
verif: Publisher announcement verified; full volume and bibliography not inspected.

title: Indigenous Knowledge Systems and Practices in the Philippines: Status and Trends — Tebtebba
status: Indigenous organization publication; publisher posting dated 2021
how: Publisher offers a dedicated IKSP status-and-trends publication.

limits: 2021 denotes the publisher page’s posting date; print edition/copyright date not independently established. Download link was not readable in this session.
verif: Correct publisher landing page verified; full text not inspected. No detailed findings attributed without access.

title: Mobilizing Indigenous knowledge, innovations and practices of the Kalanguyas’ farming systems in Tinoc, Ifugao — Tebtebba/SwedBio
status: Primary community research/pilot report; full text
context: Kalanguya communities, including Binablayan, Tinoc, Ifugao
how: Community-selected knowledge holders, interviews, group discussion and validation inform a Multiple Evidence Base approach.
use: Farming knowledge, community-led research and adaptation of knowledge systems.

title: Sustaining Our Forests, Our Rice Lands, Our Culture: Perspectives of the Pidlisan People — Tebtebba
status: Community/Indigenous organization publication; catalog description
how: Publisher describes forest and rice-land knowledge and community innovations during 2014–2020.

status: Peer-reviewed article; repository abstract/metadata inspected

title: Calderon, M.M., Bantayan, N.C., Dizon, J.T., Sajise, A.J.U., Codilan, A.L. & Canceran, M.S. — Community-based resource assessment and management planning for the rice terraces of Hungduan, Ifugao, Philippines
status: Journal article; university abstract/metadata inspected

status: Published conference abstract; not a full evaluation

title: World Bank — No Data, No Story: Indigenous Peoples in the Philippines
status: Institutional analytical report; official highlights reviewed
context: National data and socioeconomic conditions of Philippine IPs
how: Addresses data gaps and visibility of IP populations and outcomes.
use: Context for why documentation, disaggregation and community-relevant data matter.
limits: Not an IKSP manual and not an authority to classify individuals’ identity. Full report was not retrieved; claims restricted to official highlights.
verif: Official report-highlights page reviewed; full-report detailed findings not independently assessed.

title: Epanaw launch news → underlying trilogy
status: Publication located; full books not obtained
how: Followed the news to NCIP’s launch announcement, which identifies Pagkilala, Paggalang and Pagtaguyod.
use: Use PU01–PU03 as leads for community profiles, practices and livelihood contexts.
limits: News does not establish that all ICCs/IPs are comprehensively represented. Read the books and their selection/editorial methods before assessing coverage.
verif: Primary publisher: https://ncip.gov.ph/news/ncip-launching-indigenous-peoples-pagkilala-recognize-paggalang-respect-and-pagtaguyod-promote-coffee-table-books/

title: Epanaw → NCIP Annual Accomplishment Report 2021
status: Underlying official institutional publication identified
how: NCIP’s 2021 annual report corroborates the trilogy and its 14 March 2021 launch.
use: Confirms that the news refers to actual institutional publications.
limits: Annual report is evidence of the publication activity, not independent evaluation of every cultural account. Some later notices use a different launch year; prioritize contemporaneous 2021 sources.
verif: Official report indexed content verified; full volumes remain unreviewed.

title: Epanaw → university holdings/receipt

context: Carlos Hilado Memorial State University, Talisay
how: University states that NCIP turned over Epanaw books to its library, providing a concrete institutional access lead.
use: Locating actual volumes for close reading and bibliography review.
limits: Receipt notice is not a searchable national union catalog or confirmation of current loan/scan availability. No ISBN was verified.
verif: Additional receipt lead: https://www.dmmmsu.edu.ph/2023/09/19/ncip-gifts-dmmmsu-coffee-table-books/

context: Schools of Living Traditions / Buklog safeguarding
how: Followed institutional descriptions to the UNESCO Good Safeguarding Practices record and the non-formal education project identifying a two-part guide.
use: Identifies an actual programme and curriculum-documentation output behind general success stories.
limits: Full guide not retrieved; programme recognition is not proof that every SLT has equal results.

status: Underlying repository and named research reports located
how: Followed the platform’s institutional trail to DOST’s database listing and PITAHC’s research/publication catalog.
use: Distinguishes a platform announcement from individual research reports that can be appraised.

title: Indigenous Peoples’ Rights Act — Republic Act No. 8371
relevance: Section 34 recognizes Indigenous Peoples’ ownership, control and protection of their cultural and intellectual rights, including IKSP. Provides a legal foundation for examining how Indigenous knowledge is collected and used in AI, although the law does not specifically address AI. (elibrary.judiciary.gov.ph)

title: NCIP Administrative Order No. 1, series of 2012 — IKSP and Customary Laws Research and Documentation Guidelines
relevance: Addresses FPIC, collective ownership, community participation, validation, publication and benefit sharing in IKSP research and documentation. Relevant when assessing consent and safeguards for knowledge intended for digital repositories or AI applications. (wipo.int)
source: Full guidelines: NCIP PDF · WIPO text

title: CHR statement on National Indigenous Peoples Day
relevance: Explicitly discusses AI, Indigenous data sovereignty, cultural appropriation, digital exclusion, bias and surveillance. Calls for community control over how information is collected, stored, used and shared. (chr.gov.ph)
source: Full official statement: Commission on Human Rights

title: NCIP call for inclusive and culturally grounded AI development
relevance: NCIP officials called for AI policies grounded in Indigenous values and emphasized equipping and protecting Indigenous youth participating in digital transformation. This records an institutional position rather than an adopted AI regulation. (pia.gov.ph)
source: Official government report: Philippine Information Agency

title: Mindanao Natural Language Processing R&D Laboratory — DOST–UIC
relevance: Develops AI-related language tools, including machine translation and conversational agents. The initiative works with NCIP XI on Manobo, Kagan and Mansaka language preservation. Documents a practical application; long-term revitalization outcomes are not established by the announcement. (pcieerd.dost.gov.ph)

title: Digital Arang and the Kalinga Indigenous knowledge–AI governance initiative
date: Ordinance reportedly signed September 2026; repository launched 30 October 2026
relevance: KSU reports a community-governed IKSP repository with four access levels, FPIC, restrictions on unauthorized AI training and an oversight committee. Offers a local example of translating Indigenous data sovereignty into governance arrangements. (ksu.edu.ph)
source: Official institutional account: Kalinga State University. Full signed ordinance not located.

title: UNPFII study: “Indigenous Peoples and artificial intelligence” — E/C.19/2026/4, prepared by Hindou Oumarou Ibrahim
date: Issued 5 February 2026; considered at the 25th session, 24 April 2026
relevance: Examines Indigenous data sovereignty, knowledge appropriation without consent, cultural protection, digital exclusion and AI’s environmental impacts, alongside opportunities for language revitalization and knowledge transmission. Provides an international analytical reference for examining Philippine IKSP safeguards. It is a study presented to the Forum; its findings should be distinguished from formally adopted recommendations.
source: Full UN document: E/C.19/2026/4 — language selection · English PDF

title: Maddela v. Oxiana Philippines, Inc. — G.R. No. 198243, 27 February 2019. Resolution text
context: Bugkalot communities in Pao and Kakidugen, Kasibu, Nueva Vizcaya, challenged mining-exploration FPIC. Of 124 qualified household representatives, 66 voted: 60 in favour and six against.
ruling: The favourable votes were insufficient under the rules applied: consent required a majority of representatives of all households concerned, rather than those voting. The Court invalidated the documents and ordered new FPIC proceedings. Bribery allegations were not substantially proven.
government_roles:
DENR–MGB Region II — Issued the exploration permit.

NCIP regional office/FPIC team — Conducted investigation and facilitated FPIC.

NCIP Regional Hearing Office II — Earlier compelled FPIC; later dismissed the challenge.

NCIP en banc — Approved certification and subsequently dismissed the administrative appeal.

Court of Appeals (CA) — Affirmed the administrative rulings.

Supreme Court (SC) — Reversed and remanded for new proceedings.

title: Lone Congressional District of Benguet Province v. Lepanto; Republic v. Lepanto — G.R. Nos. 244063 and 244216, 21 June 2022. SC judgment
context: Renewal of a mining agreement overlapping Mankayan ancestral domains, Benguet. The companies obtained an arbitral award dispensing with FPIC and NCIP certification.
ruling: The Court vacated the award because dispensing with these safeguards violated public policy protecting Indigenous Peoples. Renewal remained subject to FPIC compliance.
government_roles:
DENR — Contracting authority and government party to arbitration.

MGB–CAR — Evaluated renewal and referred certification requirements to NCIP.

NCIP — Responsible for FPIC/certification; not impleaded in arbitration.

Makati RTC Branch 149 — Issued an injunction protecting operations pending resolution.

Makati RTC Branch 141 — Vacated the award.

CA — Reinstated it; denied intervention.

Benguet congressional district — Sought intervention and challenged its denial.

SC — Vacated the award.

Ad hoc arbitral tribunal — Issued the disputed award; not a government agency.

title: NCIP v. Macroasia Corporation — G.R. No. 226176, 9 August 2023. SC judgment
context: Mining in Brooke’s Point, Palawan, involving directly affected Pala’wan communities and indirectly affected Aribungos and Barong-barong.
ruling: The Court approved a compromise agreement, recording subsequent separate FPIC processes for the two indirectly affected barangays, and closed the case. Settlement-based outcome, rather than a broad merits ruling.
government_roles:
DENR–MGB — Processed permit applications and endorsed them to NCIP.

DENR Secretary — Approved assignment of the mining agreement.

NCIP regional office/FPIC team — Conducted initial FPIC.

Regional Review Team — Recommended validation and inclusion of indirectly affected communities.

NCIP Validation Team — Investigated and recommended certification.

NCIP en banc — Denied certification, pursued review and later compromised.

NCIP provincial/regional offices — Validated subsequent FPIC.

CA — Directed certification in its amended decision.

SC — Approved the compromise.

title: La Bugal-B’laan Tribal Association, Inc. v. Ramos — G.R. No. 127882, 1 December 2004 resolution. SC resolution
context: A B’laan association and other petitioners challenged the Mining Act, its regulations and the Western Mining financial or technical assistance agreement (FTAA).
ruling: On reconsideration, the Court reversed its January 2004 decision, upheld the challenged FTAA framework and agreement, and invalidated two agreement provisions.
government_roles:
Congress — Enacted the challenged Mining Act.

DENR Secretary — Issued implementing regulations; respondent.

MGB Director — Respondent in the challenge.

Executive Secretary — Executive-branch respondent.

Office of the Solicitor General (OSG) — Presented government arguments and sought reconsideration.

NEDA Secretary — Presented economic arguments supporting the framework, discussed in the opinions.

SC — Heard the challenge directly and reconsidered its earlier ruling.

title: Didipio Earth-Savers’ Multi-Purpose Association, Inc. v. Gozun — G.R. No. 157882, 30 March 2006. Judgment
context: Farmers and Indigenous Peoples affected by the Climax-Arimco FTAA in Nueva Vizcaya and Quirino challenged the mining framework, including taking and compensation provisions.
ruling: The Court dismissed the petition and upheld the challenged provisions. Courts retained authority to determine just compensation. This was not a finding of an FPIC violation.
government_roles:
Office of the President — President Ramos executed the FTAA; later cancellation demands reached President Arroyo.

Executive Secretary/OP Undersecretary — Named respondents; executive offices received or routed demands.

DENR — Issued regulations, received demands and referred them to MGB.

MGB Region II–Panel of Arbitrators — Required procedural compliance before acting on the referral.

MGB central office — Rejected the cancellation demand.

SC — Resolved the constitutional challenge.

title: Cruz v. Secretary of Environment and Natural Resources — G.R. No. 135385, 6 December 2000. SC resolution and opinions
context: Constitutional challenge to IPRA’s ancestral-domain and natural-resource provisions; not litigation over one mining project.
ruling: The challenge was dismissed after a 7–7 division, leaving IPRA standing. Explanations in separate opinions require appropriate attribution.
government_roles:
Congress — Enacted IPRA.

NCIP Chairperson/Commissioners — Defended constitutionality.

DENR and DBM Secretaries — Respondents submitting a consolidated comment through OSG.

OSG — Argued partial unconstitutionality, differing from NCIP.

Commission on Human Rights — Intervened in support of IPRA.

Senator Juan Flavier — Joined intervenors defending IPRA; not a separate institutional Senate action.

SC — Heard the challenge directly and dismissed it following the equal division.
